A guided path from your first print() to a portfolio project

THE METHOD

Learn by shipping, not by watching

Every week ends with something you can show someone.

Why this course

Why this course exists

Most Python courses dump syntax at you and call it teaching. We flip it: you build one small real thing per week — a quiz, a budget tracker, a tiny web scraper — and the syntax shows up exactly when you need it.

Cohorts over cramming

Cohorts over cramming

You're never alone. Every cohort has a live weekly call, a private channel, and a mentor who reviews your code within 24 hours.

The 20-minute rule

The 20-minute rule

New concept? You watch a 3-minute explainer, then practice for 20 minutes in a real editor. If you're stuck longer than 20 minutes, you ping the cohort.

What you'll build

What you'll build

Week 1: a greeting script. Week 2: a quiz game. Week 3: a budget tracker. Week 4: a weather CLI. Week 5: data analysis on real CSV. Week 6: a web scraper. Week 7: an API. Week 8: your portfolio project, deployed.

CORE DEFINITION

Idiomatic Python

/ˌɪdiəˈmætɪk ˈpaɪθən/

Code that follows the community's conventions — readable, Pythonic, and easy to maintain.

What mentors are always pushing you toward in reviews.

Before you enroll

Q1

Do I need any math background?

No. If you can add two numbers, you have enough math for this course.

Q2

How much time per week?

4-6 hours: one live call, three practice blocks, and the weekly build.

Q3

What if I fall behind?

Lifetime access plus cohort catch-up weeks — you never miss the path.

Q4

Do I get a certificate?

Yes, with your deployed portfolio project as the real proof.
